# Margo Engine: full documentation for AI tools

> Generated by scripts/build-llms.mjs from the package READMEs, api/ reports and docs/. The shorter index is llms.txt. Package READMEs longer than 5000 characters are cut; the link at the cut has the rest, and each package has an API page with every declaration.

=== Repository README (README.md) ===

# Margo Engine

A small WebGPU engine for the web, with a Rust/Wasm core.

[![CI](https://github.com/scottcampbelldata/margoengine/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/scottcampbelldata/margoengine/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/margoengine.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/margoengine)
[![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

![A textured crate and a ball with shadows on a checkered floor, rendered by Margo Engine](docs/images/quickstart.webp)

**[Quickstart: a textured, lit scene with shadows and picking in five minutes](#quickstart)** ·
[Start here: guides by goal](docs/start-here.md) · [Live demos](https://margoengine.com) ·
[Coming from three.js](docs/from-threejs.md)

The core and the stage together are 22,859 bytes gzip, Wasm kernel and WebGPU backend included. Everything else
(glTF, shadows, physics, post effects) is a separate package you import only if you use it.

## Install

Margo needs WebGPU (see [Browser support](#browser-support)). End users: Node 22.12 or newer (tested on 22.12 and the
latest 22.x, 24.18 and 26). Contributors: Node 24.18 or newer.

**The packages are not on npm yet.** `npm install margoengine` does not work today; 1.0.0 is the first planned release.
Two routes work now. Both start from a clone. The quickstart does not need the [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com) test
assets (about 270 MB), so skip them: if Git LFS is installed, set `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1` for the clone (in PowerShell,
`$env:GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1`). You need the assets only to run the tests, see [Build from source](#build-from-source).

```sh
GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone https://github.com/scottcampbelldata/margoengine.git
cd margoengine
npm ci
```

**Route 1: run the quickstart inside the clone.** Nothing to install in a project of your own.

```sh
npm run build:packages
npm run dev:examples
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:5173/examples/quickstart/>. That page is the quickstart below, saved as
[examples/quickstart/](examples/quickstart).

**Route 2: use the packages in your own project from local tarballs.** `npm run pack:packages` builds every package and
writes one `.tgz` file each to `test-results/`. Install them all, plus Vite, in a new folder (shown for a shell that
expands `*.tgz`, such as Git Bash, macOS or Linux; in PowerShell list the files or use `Get-ChildItem`):

```sh
npm run pack:packages
mkdir ../my-scene && cd ../my-scene
npm init -y
npm install ../margoengine/test-results/*.tgz vite
```

On the machine used to write this page, `npm ci` took 15 seconds, packing 35 and the install 8; from the first command
to a rendered, verified page took 76 seconds (`npm run check:quickstart` repeats the whole run and fails above 300).
Then follow the Quickstart steps 2 to 4 below in `my-scene`.

**After 1.0.0 is published,** `npm install margoengine vite` in a new folder replaces Route 2 and nothing else changes.

## Quickstart

You will build a floor, a crate and a ball with a texture, sun light, soft shadows, orbit controls and click-to-select.
It takes four steps in a new folder (or skip them and use the page from the clone above).

1. Install the packages as in Route 2 above (or use Route 1 and skip to step 4).
2. Save this as `index.html`:

```html index.html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <link rel="icon" href="data:," />
    <title>Margo Engine quickstart</title>
    <style>
      body { margin: 0; font: 16px system-ui, sans-serif }
      #scene { height: 100vh }
      #status { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 12px; margin: 0; padding: 4px 8px; background: #fffa; border-radius: 4px }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="scene"></div>
    <p id="status">Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom.</p>
    <script type="module" src="./main.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

3. Save this as `main.ts`:

```ts main.ts
import { createStage } from 'margoengine';
import { boxGeometry, planeGeometry, sphereGeometry } from 'margoengine/geometry';
import { PbrMaterial, Texture, createMesh } from 'margoengine/materials';
import { Picking, Selection } from 'margoengine/selection';
import { Shadows } from 'margoengine/shadows';

const status = document.querySelector('#status')!;
if (!('gpu' in navigator)) {
  status.textContent = 'This browser has no WebGPU, which this scene needs. See "Browser support" in the README.';
  throw new Error('WebGPU unavailable');
}

// A 64 x 64 checkerboard painted in code, so the example needs no image file.
const pixels = new Uint8Array(64 * 64 * 4);
for (let y = 0; y < 64; y++)
  for (let x = 0; x < 64; x++) {
    const light = ((x >> 3) + (y >> 3)) % 2 === 0;
    pixels.set(light ? [235, 235, 225, 255] : [70, 90, 110, 255], (y * 64 + x) * 4);
  }
const checker = new Texture({ data: pixels, width: 64, height: 64 }, { wrapS: 'repeat', wrapT: 'repeat' });

// The stage mounts a canvas in #scene, adds orbit/pan/zoom with the mouse and starts the render loop.
const stage = await createStage('#scene', { camera: { position: [4, 3, 6], target: [0, 0.6, 0] } }).catch((error: Error) => {
  status.textContent = `Margo could not start: ${error.message}. See "Browser support" in the README.`;
  throw error;
});
const engine = stage.engine;

// Aim the sun from the left and above, so the shadows fall to the right, where the camera can see them.
engine.scene.lighting.direction.set([-4, 4, 2, 3]); // x, y, z point toward the light; the last number is its strength

// Three lit, textured meshes.
const floor = new PbrMaterial({ map: checker });
floor.setUVTransform({ scale: [6, 6] }); // repeat the texture 6 times across the floor
const ground = createMesh(engine, planeGeometry(12, 12), floor);
ground.root.setRotation([-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]); // planes face +z; lay it flat
const crate = createMesh(engine, boxGeometry(1, 1, 1), new PbrMaterial({ map: checker, roughness: 0.6 }));
crate.root.setPosition([-1, 0.5, 0]);
const ball = createMesh(engine, sphereGeometry(0.6, 48, 24), new PbrMaterial({ color: '#84d6bd', roughness: 0.25 }));
ball.root.setPosition([1, 0.6, 0]);

// Shadows: tell the shadow package which meshes cast and receive.
const shadows = Shadows.attach(engine, { resolution: 2048 });
for (const mesh of [ground, crate, ball]) shadows.add(mesh);

// Click a mesh to outline it; click empty space to clear.
const picking = Picking.attach(engine);
const outline = Selection.attach(engine, { color: [1, 0.6, 0] });
const names = new Map<unknown, string>([
  [crate, 'crate'],
  [ball, 'ball'],
]);
let pressed = [0, 0];
let busy = false; // one pick can wait at a time
engine.canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', (event) => {
  pressed = [event.clientX, event.clientY];
});
engine.canvas.addEventListener('click', async (event) => {
  const moved = Math.hypot(event.clientX - pressed[0], event.clientY - pressed[1]);
  if (busy || moved > 4) return; // ignore the end of an orbit drag
  busy = true;
  const hit = await picking.pick(event.offsetX, event.offsetY);
  busy = false;
  const name = hit?.model ? names.get(hit.model) : undefined;
  outline.set(name && hit ? [hit.mesh] : []);
  status.textContent = name ? `Picked the ${name}.` : 'Click the crate or the ball.';
});

stage.onTick((delta) => {
  crate.root.rotation.y += delta * 0.5;
});
window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => stage.dispose(), { once: true });
```

4. Run `npx vite` and open the address it prints. Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan, click the crate.

If the page is blank or shows an error:

- Vite says `Failed to resolve import "margoengine"`: step 1 did not run in this folder. Run the `npm install` line from
  Route 2 again in the folder that holds `index.html` (and use `npx vite` there, not in the clone).
- The status line says `This browser has no WebGPU` or `Margo could not start`: use desktop Chrome or Edge, or see
  [Browser support](#browser-support).

The scene is about 60 lines. Three things to know about it:

- `createStage` mounts the canvas in `#scene`, adds mouse and touch camera controls and starts the render loop.
- `createMesh` (from `margoengine/materials`) draws a geometry with a `PbrMaterial`. That is how a mesh gets a
  texture. `stage.box()` and `stage.sphere()` make plain-colour meshes with no texture.
- Shadows, picking and outlines are separate packages. You import them when you want them and pay nothing when you do not.

**WebGPU and the fallback.** This scene needs WebGPU. Chrome and Edge on desktop are the browsers the engine is tested
in. Without WebGPU the page shows a message and stops. The site's demos run on WebGL2 without WebGPU through the optional
[`@margoengine/webgl2-compat`](packages/webgl2-compat/README.md) layer. The small [`@margoengine/webgl`](packages/webgl/README.md)
preview renders plain meshes with flat shading on WebGL2, with no textures, shadows, effects or picking, so it cannot run this
quickstart. Details are under [Browser support](#browser-support).

Next: [Start here](docs/start-here.md) lists a guide for each goal: [textures and materials](docs/guides/textures-and-materials.md),
[lights and shadows](docs/guides/lights-and-shadows.md), [camera and controls](docs/guides/camera-and-controls.md),
[interaction](docs/guides/interaction.md), [loading glTF](docs/guides/loading-gltf.md) and
[animation](docs/guides/animation.md).

## Build from source

You need Node.js 24.18+ (the repository's tests need it; the packages you build run on Node 22.12+) and
[Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com) for the test assets.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/scottcampbelldata/margoengine.git
cd margoengine
git lfs install
git lfs pull
npm ci
npm test
```

`npm test` builds every package from the checked-in Wasm and runs the unit tests. You don't need Rust unless you
change the kernel.

```sh
npm run dev               # Night Citadel showcase
npm run dev:examples      # every page in examples/, e.g. /examples/flight-helmet.html
npm run lint              # Biome
npm run typecheck         # strict TypeScript for all packages
npm run test:all          # every Node test in the repo
npm run test:kernel       # Rust kernel tests (toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml)
npm run measure:size      # core + stage size check
```

## Features

- WebGPU renderer with PBR, image-based lighting, cascaded shadows, clustered lights, SSAO, bloom, TAA and depth of
  field. Each one is its own package.
- Rust/Wasm transform kernel with GPU culling and instancing.
- Loaders for glTF/GLB (Draco, Meshopt, KTX2), FBX, USDZ, OBJ, STL, PLY, 3MF, COLLADA, IFC and more.
- Camera controls with CAD-style mouse presets, a view cube, GPU picking and selection outlines.
- Skinning, morph targets, blend trees and IK.
- Physics on Rapier, navmesh, ECS, input and audio.
- Terrain, water, sky, procedural scenery, voxels and a progressive voxel path tracer.
- React 18 and 19 components (`@margoengine/react`).
- Optional WebGL2 fallback: the compatibility layer runs the site's demos, the small preview draws basic scenes.

More examples are in [examples/](examples/README.md).

## Browser support

Margo Engine needs WebGPU. Without it, the optional `@margoengine/webgl2-compat` layer runs the WebGPU code of core and the
packages on WebGL2 (every site demo loads it; [docs/webgl2-compat-demos.md](docs/webgl2-compat-demos.md) lists how each one compares with native).
Or pass the `@margoengine/webgl` fallback to get a basic WebGL2 preview of plain meshes (no textures, effects or picking),
which stays for v1.0.

| Browser | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome and Edge (desktop) | Tested. The browser suites run in Chromium on a real GPU (Intel Arc 140V) and on SwiftShader in the manual browser workflow. |
| Safari on iPhone | Demos run, checked by hand only. |
| Safari on macOS | Has WebGPU, not tested. |
| Firefox | Not tested. |
| Android | Not tested. |

[docs/limits.md](docs/limits.md) lists the hardware these results come from and what has not been checked.

## Size

| Bundle | gzip | raw |
| --- | --- | --- |
| core + stage (`import { createStage } from 'margoengine'`) | 22,859 B | 56,738 B |

Recorded in [entry-sizes.json](examples/package-benchmarks/results/entry-sizes.json), along with
the size of every other package entry. `npm run measure:size` bundles the entry with Vite, minified the same way as
the package build, gzips it at the default level and prints the figure for your checkout. The build fails if
core + stage reaches 25,000 B gzip.

`npm run bench` runs the render, load, assembly, physics and memory suites with medians, p95 and machine checks. See
[docs/benchmarking.md](docs/benchmarking.md). No comparisons with other engines are published here yet.

## Architecture

```
your app
  margoengine            createStage: canvas, camera, controls, loading
  @margoengine/core      Engine, Scene, Mesh, Geometry, PbrMaterial; WebGPU renderer
    kernel (Rust/Wasm)   transforms, bounds and culling in one flat buffer
  @margoengine/*         optional packages, attached through core's extension hooks
```

Core is frozen: packages add render passes, materials and loaders through `@margoengine/core/extension` instead of
changing the base, so the base stays small and an app only pays for what it imports. The Rust source is in
`packages/kernel`; the compiled Wasm is checked in, so building the JavaScript never needs Rust.

[MODERN-ENGINE.md](MODERN-ENGINE.md) covers the architecture, lifecycle rules and limits in detail.
[docs/api-overview.md](docs/api-overview.md) is a short tour of the API. AI coding tools can read
[margoengine.com/llms.txt](https://margoengine.com/llms.txt) or run the `@margoengine/mcp` server
([docs/ai-tools.md](docs/ai-tools.md)).

98 packages in 12 layers, the same as the [catalog](https://margoengine.com/catalog/).

### Start here (3)

| Package | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`margoengine`](packages/margoengine/README.md) | Margo Engine in one install: the stage and every package as margoengine/<name> (margoengine/gltf, margoengine/shadows, margoengine/physics, margoengine/react). |
| [`@margoengine/stage`](packages/stage/README.md) | The stage: createStage mounts a canvas, camera controls and rendering in five lines. Re-exported by margoengine. |
| [`@margoengine/core`](packages/core/README.md) | WebGPU rendering and a Wasm transform kernel. WebGL2 is the optional @margoengine/webgl package. |

### Setup and diagnostics (6)

| Package | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`@margoengine/math`](packages/math/README.md) | Vector, quaternion, matrix, Euler, color, bounds, ray, plane and frustum math, one module per type. |
| [`@margoengine/quality`](packages/quality/README.md) | Measured quality tiers: start light, time the GPU, remember full 4x quality only where it has headroom. |
| [`@margoengine/webgl`](packages/webgl/README.md) | WebGL2 fallback renderer for browsers without WebGPU: flat-shaded PBR core meshes, opt in with Engine.create(canvas, {fallback: webglRenderer}). |
| [`@margoengine/webgl2-compat`](packages/webgl2-compat/README.md) | The WebGL2 compatibility layer for browsers without WebGPU (milestones M0 to M8 done); the site's demos run on it there. install() gives core a WebGPU-shaped device on WebGL2 that translates WGSL to GLSL ES 3.00; render shaders, texture views, readbacks of every copyable format, occlusion queries, render bundles, external textures, gather and storage-buffer reads run, compute pipelines run as fragment draws, point draws or on the CPU, whichever the shader allows, and DOF, splats and culling take routes of their own there. The voxel path tracer and XR refuse it. |
| [`@margoengine/stats`](packages/stats/README.md) | Allocation-free frame samples, DOM performance overlay and optional WebGPU timestamp profiling. |
| [`@margoengine/inspector`](packages/inspector/README.md) | Entity hierarchy, live properties, WebGPU wireframe, normal and bounding-box overlays, and a frame debugger. |

| [`@margoengine/text`](packages/text/README.md) | GPU signed distance field text for Margo Engine: runtime glyph atlases from any browser font, wrapping, alignment, outlines and shadows, WebGPU. |

| [`@margoengine/vfx`](packages/vfx/README.md) | GPU particle simulation and indirect billboards, with curves over life and sphere, cone and mesh-surface emitters. |
| [`@margoengine/creative`](packages/creative/README.md) | WebGPU particles, atmosphere, toon shading and post-processing for Margo Engine. |
| [`@margoengine/procedural`](packages/procedural/README.md) | Procedural cabins, foliage, grass, humanoids, Marching Cubes surfaces, seeded 2D/3D/4D noise, L-systems, Voronoi fracture and a bounded voxel expression language. |
| [`@margoengine/wfc`](packages/wfc/README.md) | Seeded wave function collapse: 3D tile adjacency and the 2D overlapping (sample-based) model with backtracking. |
| [`@margoengine/splines`](packages/splines/README.md) | 3D Catmull-Rom, Bezier, Hermite, B-spline and Kochanek-Bartels curves with arc-length lookup, closest point, stable frames and knot editing. |

## Roadmap

- Publish 1.0.0 to npm.
- The WebGL2 compatibility layer is an optional package that WebGPU users never load ([docs/webgl2-compat-roadmap.md](docs/webgl2-compat-roadmap.md)); the voxel path tracer and XR refuse it. `@margoengine/webgl` is the small preview; in the React Canvas, `loadFallback` loads it and `fallbackContent` replaces the plain message.
- Testing on more hardware: Apple silicon, AMD, Android, Firefox and macOS Safari.
- Published benchmark comparisons with their method and raw results.

=== API overview (docs/api-overview.md) ===

# API overview

A short tour. Each package README has the full reference. The public API of every entry point is recorded in
[`api/`](../api), and `npm run api:check` fails when it changes by accident.

## Three levels

| Level | Import | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stage | `margoengine` (`@margoengine/stage`) | You want a canvas, a camera, controls and loading in a few lines. |
| Engine | `@margoengine/core` | You manage the canvas, the frame loop and the scene yourself. |
| Packages | `@margoengine/<name>` or `margoengine/<name>` | You need a feature that is not in core. |

`margoengine/<name>` is a one-line re-export of `@margoengine/<name>`. Import either; the bundles are the same.

## Stage

```ts
import { createStage, Geometry } from 'margoengine';
import { addGLTF } from 'margoengine/stage/gltf';

const stage = await createStage('#scene', { controls: true, autoStart: true, onError: console.error });

stage.box({ size: [1, 1, 1], color: '#84d6bd', position: [0, 0.5, 0] });
stage.sphere({ radius: 0.5, metalness: 1, roughness: 0.2 });
stage.mesh(new Geometry(positions, normals, indices), { color: '#c3c9d0' });

const model = await addGLTF(stage, '/part.glb'); // glTF and GLB
stage.fit(model.meshes);

const off = stage.onTick((delta) => {}); // seconds since the last frame
stage.dispose();
```

`stage.engine` is the core `Engine` underneath.

## Engine

```ts
import { Engine, box } from '@margoengine/core';

// WebGPU; pass { fallback } from @margoengine/webgl to fall back to WebGL2
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas, { camera: { position: [0, 2, 5], target: [0, 0, 0] } });
const cube = engine.createMesh().setGeometry(box()).setPosition([0, 0.5, 0]);
engine.start();

const hit = await engine.pick(x, y); // GPU picking, a Mesh or null
engine.use(plugin); // attach a package (shadows, post effects, physics, ...)
engine.dispose();
```

Meshes are handles into the Wasm kernel's transform storage. `mesh.position`, `mesh.rotation` and `mesh.scale` are
live views, so writing to them costs no allocation. Geometry is shared: meshes with the same `Geometry` draw as one
instanced batch.

## Packages

Packages attach to an engine through plugins and the `@margoengine/core/extension` entry. They never change core, so
core stays inside its size budget no matter how many packages exist. Some examples:

```ts
import { Shadows } from 'margoengine/shadows';

const shadows = Shadows.attach(engine, { resolution: 2048 });
shadows.add(cube);
```

The [package list](../README.md#packages) and the [catalog](README.md) describe each one.

## Errors

Bad arguments throw `TypeError` or `RangeError`. Everything else throws a `MargoError` with a stable `code`:
`disposed`, `attached`, `state`, `unsupported` or `failed`. Branch on the code, not the message. The conventions are in
[conventions.md](conventions.md).

## Limits

What is supported, what is not, and where each limit is enforced: [limits.md](limits.md).

=== Package conventions (docs/conventions.md) ===

# Package conventions

Rules every Margo package follows for shared types, errors and export names.
`npm run hygiene` measures them; `scripts/hygiene-allowlist.json` holds the few justified exceptions.

## Shared types: one definition, in `@margoengine/math`

Type-only shapes used by more than one package are declared once in `@margoengine/math` (`packages/math/src/types.ts`)
and imported from there. Types are erased at build time, so this costs 0 runtime bytes.

| Type | Shape | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Vec2` | `readonly [x, y]` | 2D input points |
| `Vec3` | `readonly [x, y, z]` | 3D input points, directions, Euler angles. Declared in `@margoengine/core` (frozen, upstream of math) and re-exported by math. |
| `Vec4` | `readonly [x, y, z, w]` | homogeneous points, RGBA |
| `Quat` | `readonly [x, y, z, w]` | unit quaternions (`setQuaternion`) |
| `MutableVec2`, `MutableVec3` | `[x, y]`, `[x, y, z]` | freshly allocated results the caller may modify (geometry curves, `@margoengine/math/vec3`) |
| `Mat4` | `ArrayLike<number>` | column-major 4x4 (`camera.matrix`, world matrices) |
| `ColorInput` | `string \| number \| readonly number[]` | `'#rrggbb'`, `'#rgb'`, `0xrrggbb` (sRGB), CSS `'color(display-p3 r g b)'` (also `srgb`, `srgb-linear`, `display-p3-linear`) or linear sRGB `[r, g, b]`; decode with `parseColor`. A P3 colour outside sRGB decodes to negative linear sRGB channels and keeps them; linear arrays must stay non-negative. Light colours (clustered, area, directional) may be negative per channel with a luminance of 0 or more; core's sun takes only sRGB, so give it `clipToSRGB(rgb)`. |
| `HeightField` | `(x, z) => number` | ground height samplers |
| `Vec2Like`, `Vec3Like`, `Vec4Like` | `{x, y}`, `{x, y, z}`, `{x, y, z, w}` | object-shaped input (`mesh.position`, navigation path endpoints) |
| `SphereLike`, `PlaneLike`, `BoxLike` | `{center, radius}`, `{normal, constant}`, `{min, max}` | structural input of the bounds classes |

Rules:

- Readonly tuples for input, `Mutable*` for results the caller owns. A mutable tuple is accepted wherever the readonly
  one is.
- A package that keeps a public name for one of these re-exports it (`export type { Vec3 } from '@margoengine/math'`),
  never redeclares it.
- A package whose public `.d.ts` uses a math type, or that throws `MargoError`, lists `@margoengine/math` under
  `dependencies` (consumers need it for the types). Bundling is the build script's choice: `scripts/build-optional.js`
  keeps dependencies external (one shared copy at runtime); packages with their own build scripts (lines, points,
  text, geometry) bundle the math helpers they use, as before. Exception: a package whose build inlines math (the
  default `build-modern` pipeline, `build-postfx.js`, creative's script) and whose `.d.ts` uses no math type keeps math
  under `devDependencies` (build order only; consumers never load it): post, clustered, shadows, taa, splats, creative,
  dof, tonemap. The tonemap test pins "no `dependencies`".
- A private alias that shows up in a published `.d.ts` (`type Context = Extract<PassContext, {backend: 'webgpu'}>`)
  is still a declaration there: give it a package-specific name (`SkyPassContext`, `PostPassContext`, ...) rather
  than the same name in many packages. Core (frozen) cannot host a shared one.

## Errors

| Situation | Throw |
| --- | --- |
| An argument has the wrong type or shape, or a node is used in the wrong shader stage | `TypeError` |
| A value is out of range, non-finite, or over a limit | `RangeError` |
| Anything else | `MargoError` with a `code` |

`MargoError` (`import { MargoError } from '@margoengine/math'`, or `@margoengine/math/errors`) extends `Error` with
`name = 'MargoError'` and a stable `code`:

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `disposed` | used after `dispose()` |
| `attached` | already attached to, or owned by, another engine, plugin or renderer |
| `state` | not valid right now: re-entrant call from a callback, missing prerequisite, stale handle |
| `unsupported` | the browser or device lacks something needed: WebGPU, OffscreenCanvas, a shader hook |
| `failed` | the operation ran and produced no result: no solution within the budget, a failed request |
| `timeout` | a step that should finish never settled within its time limit: a stalled WebGPU startup step |

Branch on `error.code`, not on the message. Messages name the subject, the problem and the fix, in that order:
`'Input is disposed; create a new Input'`. Packages bundle their own copy of the class, so `MargoError` matches by
name (`static [Symbol.hasInstance]`): `error instanceof MargoError` holds for any package's copy. Do not subclass it.
`@margoengine/loaders` has its own `LoaderError` (format plus code) for malformed input.
Likewise `@margoengine/procedural/expression` throws `VoxelExpressionError` (code `syntax`, `limit` or `evaluation`, with
the 1-based line and column) for faults in the expression text; its arguments follow the table above.

`packages/shared` is copied into packages that may not depend on math, so it cannot import the class: it throws
`margoError(code, message)` from `packages/shared/errors.js`, which builds the same shape (name `MargoError`, `code`).

### Short messages with a help link

Core and the stage facade follow the same table, but keep messages short and link each to its entry on
[margoengine.com/errors](https://margoengine.com/errors), where the cause and the fix are written out: they throw
`fault(code, message, anchor?)`, `typeError(message, anchor)` and `rangeError(message, anchor)` from
`packages/shared/errors.js` (bundled into their dist), which append `; see https://margoengine.com/errors#<anchor>`
(the anchor defaults to the code). The page is generated from `scripts/errors/entries.js` (`node
scripts/errors/page.mjs`); `tests/errors-page.test.js` checks that every link points at an entry, that every
MargoError code has one, and that the page matches the file. The quality gate counts a linked message as naming its
fix, and a link to a missing entry as naming none.

Packages may follow the same pattern: a short message, the same helpers, and their entries on the same page (add them
to `scripts/errors/entries.js`, one entry per message family). A package message without a link must name its fix
itself, as the table above says.

## Core freeze

`@margoengine/core` and the stage facade are frozen for v1.0.0 against new features, not against bug fixes (since
2026-10-24). A bug, an unsafe API (a throw that cannot be branched on, a race, a leak) or a message that names no fix
is fixed in core, with a test, inside the 25,000-byte core + stage gzip gate; record the bytes it costs. New
capabilities go in optional packages, and a fix that would add a capability is listed for the maintainer instead.

**Exception, the stage facade (Scott, 2026-10-27):** the stage is lifted from the freeze for one restructuring,
because it broke "pay only for what you import" and nothing is published yet, so no user is broken. Its ten
optional-package methods (`load`, `gltf`, `creative`, `scenery`, `sky`, `particles`, `effects`,
`environment`, `shadows`) held `import()`s that every app building a `Stage` reached (class methods are never
tree-shaken), so webpack and Turbopack failed on uninstalled optional peers. They moved into feature entries that take
the stage (`@margoengine/stage/gltf` `addGLTF`, `/sky` `addSky`, `/particles` `addParticles`,
`/effects` `addEffects`, `/environment` `addEnvironment`, `/shadows` `addShadows`; the whole-pack accessors became a
plain `import()`), and the root gained `stage.signal`. The stage root shrank (core + stage 22,781 -> 21,910 B gzip).
Core is untouched. The exception covers this one change; the freeze applies again after it.

**Exception, `powerPreference` (Scott, 2026-10-29, "do the core add i agree"):** core gains one option,
`EngineOptions.powerPreference` (`'low-power'` | `'high-performance'`), which `GPURenderer.create` passes to
`requestAdapter` at creation and again on device restore, so an app can pick the integrated or discrete GPU on a
two-GPU PC. Unset keeps the old request (`'high-performance'`, nothing on Windows). Cost: core 21,077 -> 21,106 B gzip, core + stage 22,494 -> 22,524 B. The exception
covers this one option; the freeze applies again after it.

**Exception, one render pass for a package's frame (Scott, 2026-11-05: core may change if justified, documented and under the
size limit):** `FramePass.joins` and the context's `attach` let a package's pass take core's clear and resolve (perf-history
entry 51). No package can hold this: core owns the clear, the resolve target and the graph's order. Cost: core + stage
22,522 -> 22,815 B gzip. The exception covers this one change; the freeze applies again after it.

## Names exported by more than one package

A name declared and exported by two packages must mean the same thing, or be renamed. Decisions:

| Name | Packages | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add`, `sub`, `dot`, `cross`, `length`, `normalize`, `clamp`, `smoothstep` | math, shader (`dot` also compute) | Kept: math's work on CPU numbers/arrays (three.js `MathUtils` names), shader's build GPU nodes (WGSL/TSL names), compute's `dot` multiplies GPU arrays (NumPy's name). Note the argument orders differ for `smoothstep`: math `(x, min, max)`, shader `(low, high, x)` as WGSL. Allowlisted. |
| `fbm`, `ridged`, `domainWarp` | procedural, shader | Kept: CPU noise and its GPU twin in `@margoengine/shader/noise` share names on purpose. Allowlisted. |
| `multiplyMatrices` | math, animation | math's `multiplyMatrices(a, b, out)` (out = a * b, `out` last like every math helper) is canonical. animation's `(out, a, b)` wrapper is removed or renamed by group B. |
| `parseColor`, `ColorInput`, `meshWorldMatrix`, `Mat4` | lines, points, text | One definition in math (`math/color`, `math/mesh`, `math`); import it from there (the packages no longer re-export `meshWorldMatrix`). |
| `Input`, `Stage`, `TextureSource` (shader) | input, margoengine, materials, points | Shader's renamed: `NodeInput`, `ShaderStage`, `BindableTexture`. |
| `projectPoint`, `PickHit`, `Blending`, `TextureSource` (points) | labels, selection, materials, shader | Points' renamed: `projectToPixels`, `PointsPickHit`, `PointsBlending`, `PointsTextureSource`. |
| `smoothstep` (tween) | math, shader | Tween's easing renamed `easeSmoothstep`. |
| `ExpandOptions` | lines, procedural | lines' renamed `ExpandLineOptions` (its function is `expandLine`). |
| `Vector3` (navmesh/build) | math | `Navigation` takes math's `Vec3Like`; math's `Vector3` is the class. |
| `loadGLTF`, `parseGLTF` | gltf, gltf-pro | Open, group B. |
| `texture` (vfx) | shader | vfx's `@margoengine/vfx/texture` feature object renamed `textureFeature` (pass `{texture: textureFeature}`); shader's `texture()` node keeps the name. |
| `Environment`, `Sky`, `Bloom`, `SSAO`, `GTAO`, `SSR`, `SSGI`, `MotionBlur`, `LensFlare`, `SMAA`, `FXAA`, `Glitch`, `Afterimage`, `TAA`, `Tonemap`, `Shadows`, `AmbientLight`, `HemisphereLight`, `Fog`, `Scene`, `RenderView`, `BatchedMesh`, `DepthTexture`, `SceneTargets`, `OrbitControls`, `MapControls`, `ArcballControls` | environment, sky, post, taa, tonemap, shadows, core, materials, controls; react | Kept: the plugin or pass class and react's JSX component that adds it with the same options (React names components after what they render). Allowlisted. |
| `Vec3` (lod), `Color` (sky, terrain), `HeightField` (terrain) | math | Math's: lod uses `MutableVec3` / `Vec3`, sky and terrain colours are `Vec3`, terrain re-exports math's `HeightField`. |
| `PbrMaterial` | core, materials, react | Kept, one meaning: materials' `PbrMaterial` takes every core `PbrMaterial` option with the same meaning and adds maps and physical options, with a textured material's defaults (white, roughness 1, metalness 0, front side) rather than core's indigo double-sided placeholder; core's stays the constant-colour material of core meshes, and react's is the JSX element that builds core's. Allowlisted. |

## Quality gate

`npm run quality` (`scripts/quality-gate.mjs`, part of `npm run verify` and CI, about 6.5 s after a build) runs five
ratchets over `packages/`. Each has a baseline of today's known violations in `scripts/quality/baselines/<gate>.json`:
a gate passes on what its baseline records and fails on anything new or worse, naming the fix.

| Gate | Items | Fails when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sizes` | gzip budget per entry and worker (entry-sizes.json's method; budget = size + max(3%, 256 B)); `leak` = an entry that statically loads another package's entry of 10,000 B or more (core and math excepted) | an entry is over its budget or new; a new static leak (use `import()` instead) |
| `duplicates` | duplicated lines per package pair (6-line normalised windows, our own detector); `family` = a known algorithm copy (CRC table, GGX, hidden-ancestor walk, ...); `reexport` = a runtime value re-exported from another package | more copied lines, a new copy or a new re-export: move the code to one package or `packages/shared` |
| `tests` | a package without a verify test; an entry no test imports | a new package or entry without a test that imports it |
| `api` | from `npm run hygiene`: undocumented public export; `throw new Error(`; a throw message that names no fix (Errors, above) | a new one of each. `tests/api-conventions.test.js` keeps attach / dispose / `Symbol.dispose` at 0 with no baseline |
| `clean-room` | mentions of three.js, Babylon or another graphics library anywhere in `packages/**`; third-party `dependencies` / `peerDependencies` | a new mention (put comparisons in docs/ or benchmarks/) or a new third-party dependency |

Baselines only shrink. When you fix a violation the gate fails until you lock it in:
`npm run quality -- --gate=<gate> --update`. Growing a baseline (a new entry's budget, an accepted dependency) needs
`npm run quality -- --gate=<gate> --update --reason="why"`; the reason is appended to the file's `history`. Size budgets
only suggest shrinking. `--summary` prints the biggest offenders; `--details` writes every item and duplicate block to
`test-results/quality.json`.

## Browser suites end with `closeAll`

A script that starts a browser must end it through `closeAll` from `scripts/support/shutdown.mjs` (bug 30, bug 70): the
browser context and browser first, then the servers' connections, the servers, and the child processes' trees, all inside
one budget that throws `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` naming what was still open. A plain `server.close()` waits for every
connection a browser holds, so a suite that passed every assertion could hang on its cleanup for ever. `launchBrowser`,
`openBrowser` and `startDevServer` already close that way. `tests/browser-teardown.test.js` (part of `npm run verify`)
fails for any script that starts a browser and an HTTP server of its own without `closeAll`.

=== A mobile-first architectural walkthrough in ~50 lines (docs/guides/walkthrough.md) ===

# A mobile-first architectural walkthrough in ~50 lines

Load a house, walk through it at eye height on a phone or a desktop, and lift the roof off into an orbit
"dollhouse" view and back. No physics engine and no WebAssembly: `WalkControls` (`@margoengine/controls/walk`)
collides against the same CPU triangle trees the `@margoengine/bvh` Raycaster uses.

<!-- Every ```ts block in this file is type-checked against the built packages by tests/from-threejs-snippets.test.js. -->

## The page

```html
<!doctype html>
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover">
<style>
  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: #000; }
  canvas { display: block; width: 100vw; height: 100dvh; user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; }
  #view { position: fixed; right: 16px; bottom: calc(16px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); font: 16px system-ui; padding: 12px 18px; }
  #hint { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; top: 16px; text-align: center; color: #fff; font: 15px system-ui; pointer-events: none; }
</style>
<canvas></canvas><button id="view">Dollhouse</button><p id="hint"></p>
<script type="module" src="./main.ts"></script>
```

## The script

```ts
import {Engine} from '@margoengine/core';
import {applyQualityTier, paceEngine, watchQuality} from '@margoengine/quality';
import {loadGLTF} from '@margoengine/gltf-pro';
import {computePrimitiveBVHAsync} from '@margoengine/bvh';
import {CameraProjection} from '@margoengine/cameras';
import {WalkControls} from '@margoengine/controls/walk';

applyQualityTier();                                    // phone, light or high tier; before the engine exists
const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
// Start on the deck, eye 1.65 m above it (y = 0), looking at the front door.
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas, {camera: {position: [2.5, 1.65, -2], target: [2.5, 1.65, 0]}});
paceEngine(engine);

const house = await loadGLTF(engine, '/assets/house.glb');
// Build the collision trees in a worker, so the first steps into a big room never stall.
await Promise.all(house.primitives.map(primitive => computePrimitiveBVHAsync(primitive)));

const projection = CameraProjection.attach(engine, {mode: 'perspective'}); // the dollhouse turns orthographic
const walk = WalkControls.attach(engine, {colliders: [house], projection});
walk.dollhouseBounds = house.bounds;                   // frame the house, not the garden around it
walk.speed = 1.4;                                      // m/s; Shift or the gamepad's left stick button runs

const button = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#view')!;
button.onclick = () => walk.toggleDollhouse();
walk.addEventListener('mode', () => {button.textContent = walk.mode === 'walk' ? 'Dollhouse' : 'Walk';});

const hint = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#hint')!;
hint.textContent = matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches ? 'Left thumb walks, right thumb looks' : 'Click to look, WASD to walk';
canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', () => hint.remove(), {once: true});

engine.start();
watchQuality();
```

## What you get

- **Eye height held by the floor.** Nine vertical rays (the centre and a ring at 0.9 × the 0.25 m radius) find the
  highest walkable floor within `stepHeight` (0.19 m): hardwood, a 12 mm rug and a deck with 1 cm gaps all keep the eye
  1.65 m above the surface, and a gap narrower than about 0.41 m (1.66 × the radius, in any direction) is stepped over instead of fallen into.
- **Stairs and steps.** Risers up to 0.19 m are climbed and the eye eases up and down them (no jumps of more than
  6 cm per frame in the tests); a taller step stops you. Floors steeper than `maxSlope` (45°) are not walkable.
- **Walls, counters and glass.** A capsule from the step height to the top of the head slides along walls and around
  door jambs, and blocks at counters. It moves in sub-steps of at most half its radius, so even a single-quad glass
  pane is never crossed (tested at 30 m/s and 10 frames per second).
- **Input.** WASD or arrows (Shift runs, C crouches); click for pointer-lock mouse look, or drag; a gamepad's sticks;
  on touch screens the left half of the canvas is a floating thumbstick (drawn where the thumb lands) and the right
  half drag-looks. Speed eases in and out (`acceleration`). For anything else (an `@margoengine/input` action, a
  custom on-screen stick) write to `walk.axes` each frame.
- **Dollhouse.** `toggleDollhouse()` eases the camera out to an orbit view of `dollhouseBounds` (or of every collider)
  facing the way you were looking, hands the canvas to `walk.orbit` (an `OrbitControls`), and eases back to exactly
  where you stood. With a `CameraProjection` the dollhouse is orthographic.
- **Large sites.** With a `FloatingOrigin` from `@margoengine/cameras/origin`, pass it as `origin` so the saved walk
  pose follows a rebase: `WalkControls.attach(engine, {origin})`.
- **Games.** `walk.jumpSpeed = 4` enables Space (gamepad A) jumps under `gravity`; ceilings stop the head.

## Cost

Measured, not estimated (records in `examples/package-benchmarks/results/`):

- **Bytes.** `walk-size.json`: WalkControls, including the OrbitControls it uses for the dollhouse, is about 12 kB
  min+gzip, about 22 kB when the app does not already ship `@margoengine/bvh`. `@margoengine/physics` plus Rapier
  (`@dimforge/rapier3d-compat` 0.21.0, Wasm inlined) is about 1.65 MB gzip (4.3 MB raw); Rapier's Wasm alone is 3.1 MB
  raw. Rapier stays the upgrade path for rigid bodies, joints and vehicles.
- **CPU.** `walk-cpu.json` (`node examples/package-benchmarks/walk-cpu.mjs`; Node, one thread, a laptop with other
  work running, so read it as an order of magnitude): `update()` takes a median of 0.01-0.03 ms and at most 0.9 ms a
  frame on the generated two-storey house, a block of 16 such houses (912 meshes) and the 2.45-million-triangle
  conveyor GLB once their trees exist. The first visit to a big part builds its tree on that frame (up to 57 ms on the
  conveyor); the worker build above avoids that.

## Limits

- The dollhouse orbits the whole model, roof included; hide the roof meshes (`mesh.visible = false`) for a cutaway.
  Hidden meshes do not collide.
- Static levels: colliders are read from the last rendered frame's matrices, so a moving door collides one frame late,
  and a platform that moves does not carry the walker.
- The capsule's sides are tested exactly against triangles; floors come from the nine rays, so on a slope the eye can
  sit up to 0.9 × radius × the slope's tangent higher (2 cm on a 1:12 ramp), and a ledge holds you until the whole
  ring is past it.
- Skinned and morphed glTF meshes collide in their bind pose (as the Raycaster hits them); alpha-masked foliage and
  transparent glass collide like solid triangles.
- A primitive's tree is built on the first frame the walker comes near it; with a big model that first frame can take
  tens of milliseconds, which `computePrimitiveBVHAsync` (above) moves to a worker.

=== Which import do I need? (docs/guides/imports.md) ===

# Which import do I need?

One install covers everything:

```bash
npm i margoengine
```

Then import what you use. Every package is a subpath of `margoengine`: `margoengine/shadows` is the package
`@margoengine/shadows`, the same module and the same classes. An app bundles only what it imports, however many
packages are installed. For a ready-made set, import a [kit](kits.md) instead (`margoengine/game`, `/viz`,
`/web`).

<!-- Every ```ts block in this file is type-checked against the built packages by tests/from-threejs-snippets.test.js.
     Snippets may use the ambient names engine, canvas, mesh and model. -->

## Start

`margoengine` itself is the stage: a canvas, camera controls and rendering in one call, plus everything the core
engine exports (`Engine`, `Mesh`, `PbrMaterial`, `box`, ...).

```ts
import {createStage} from 'margoengine';

const stage = await createStage('#viewport');
const cube = stage.box({color: '#84d6bd'});
stage.onTick((delta) => {
  cube.rotation.y += delta;
});
```

## I want to...

| Task | Import |
| --- | --- |
| Show a scene with orbit controls | `createStage` from `margoengine` |
| Use the engine without the stage | `Engine` from `margoengine` (or `margoengine/core`) |
| Load a glTF/GLB model with PBR materials | `loadGLTF` from `margoengine/gltf-pro` |
| Load a static glTF model, smallest code | `loadGLTF` from `margoengine/gltf` |
| Load FBX, USDZ, OBJ, STL, PLY, Collada ... | `margoengine/fbx`, `margoengine/usdz`, `margoengine/loaders` |
| Export glTF, STL, OBJ, USDZ | `margoengine/exporters` |
| Image-based lighting, fog, backgrounds | `margoengine/environment` |
| Many point, spot and area lights | `Clustered` from `margoengine/clustered` |
| Shadows from the sun | `Shadows` from `margoengine/shadows` |
| A physical sky with day and night | `Sky` from `margoengine/sky` |
| Materials: textures, toon, clearcoat, node graphs | `margoengine/materials`, `margoengine/shader` |
| Orbit, walk, fly or a transform gizmo | `margoengine/controls/orbit`, `/controls/walk`, `margoengine/controls`, `/controls/transform` |
| CAD navigation (SolidWorks, Inventor, Fusion ... mouse) | `cadControls` from `margoengine/controls/orbit` |
| Skeletal animation and morph targets | `Animation` from `margoengine/animation`, `Animator` from `margoengine/animator` |
| Rigid-body physics | `Physics` from `margoengine/physics`, and `npm i @dimforge/rapier3d-compat` |
| Bloom, SSAO, depth of field, anti-aliasing | `PostStack` from `margoengine/post/stack`, effects from `margoengine/post/<effect>`, `margoengine/dof` |
| Tone mapping | `Tonemap` from `margoengine/tonemap` |
| Particles | `VFX` from `margoengine/vfx` |
| Text and labels | `margoengine/text`, `margoengine/labels`, `margoengine/html` |
| Lines, grids and helpers | `margoengine/lines` |
| Point clouds and Gaussian splats | `margoengine/points`, `margoengine/splats` |
| Sound | `margoengine/audio` |
| Keyboard, mouse, gamepad and touch | `Input` from `margoengine/input` |
| Voxel worlds | `margoengine/voxel`, `margoengine/voxel-edit`, `margoengine/voxel-net` |
| React components | `margoengine/react`, and `npm i react react-dom` |
| A WebGL2 fallback for browsers without WebGPU | `margoengine/webgl` |

Every package and entry is in the [package catalog](../README.md); each package's README shows its entries as
`margoengine/<name>/<entry>` imports.

## Several packages together

```ts
import {createStage} from 'margoengine';
import {loadGLTF} from 'margoengine/gltf-pro';
import {EnvironmentLighting} from 'margoengine/environment';
import {Shadows} from 'margoengine/shadows';

const stage = await createStage('#viewport', {backend: 'webgpu'});
await EnvironmentLighting.load(stage.engine, '/studio.hdr');
const helmet = await loadGLTF(stage.engine, '/SciFiHelmet.glb');
const shadows = Shadows.attach(stage.engine, {resolution: 2048});
shadows.add(helmet);
```

## Short names

Namespace imports work and tree-shake the same as named imports in Vite, webpack, esbuild and Rollup: only the members
you use are kept.

```ts
import * as M from 'margoengine';
import * as Post from 'margoengine/post/stack';
import * as Bloom from 'margoengine/post/bloom';

const stage = await M.createStage('#viewport');
const meshes: M.Mesh[] = [stage.sphere({color: '#ffcc66'})];
Post.PostStack.attach(stage.engine, [new Bloom.Bloom({strength: 0.6})]);
console.log(meshes.length);
```

## No bundler: an import map from a CDN

Every entry is a plain ES module, so a page can load Margo straight from a CDN with an import map.
`margoengine/dist/importmap.json` maps every `margoengine` and `@margoengine/*` entry (568 of them) to jsDelivr;
copy it into the page, or only the lines your imports reach:

```html
<script type="importmap">
  {
    "imports": {
      "margoengine": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/margoengine@1.0.0/dist/index.js",
      "@margoengine/stage": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@margoengine/stage@1.0.0/dist/index.js",
      "@margoengine/core": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@margoengine/core@1.0.0/dist/index.js",
      "@margoengine/core/extension": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@margoengine/core@1.0.0/dist/extension.js"
    }
  }
</script>
<div id="viewport" style="height: 100vh"></div>
<script type="module">
  import {createStage} from 'margoengine';
  const stage = await createStage('#viewport');
  stage.box({color: '#84d6bd'});
</script>
```

`scripts/bundler-matrix.mjs` loads the packed packages this way in a browser, and builds the same app with Vite,
webpack, esbuild, Rollup and Next.js (webpack and Turbopack), checking each bundle holds only the packages it imports.

## Rules

- Import only the entries listed in the package READMEs. There are no deep imports into `dist/`: the `exports` maps
  allow only the published entries, with their types.
- Every entry is free of side effects. Nothing runs at import time; nothing is registered globally.
- `margoengine/<name>` and `@margoengine/<name>` are the same module. Mixing them in one app is fine; there is only
  ever one copy of each class.
- A heavier feature can load when it is first used: `await import('margoengine/physics')`.

## Coming from three.js

| three.js | Margo Engine |
| --- | --- |
| `npm i three` | `npm i margoengine` |
| `import * as THREE from 'three'` | `import * as M from 'margoengine'` |
| `three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js` | `margoengine/gltf-pro` (`loadGLTF`) |
| `three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js` | `margoengine/controls/orbit` |
| `three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js` | `margoengine/post/stack` |
| `three/addons/exporters/GLTFExporter.js` | `margoengine/exporters` (`exportGLB`) |

More in [from-threejs.md](../from-threejs.md).

=== Quality tiers: one app that runs at 60 FPS on a laptop and looks its best on a fast PC (docs/guides/quality-tiers.md) ===

# Quality tiers: one app that runs at 60 FPS on a laptop and looks its best on a fast PC

**Problem.** The same scene runs at 120 FPS on a desktop GPU, 40 FPS on a laptop's integrated GPU, and somewhere in
between on a phone. Guessing from the device name picks the wrong settings.

**Recipe.** Let `@margoengine/quality` measure the GPU and pick a tier, and let the feature packages scale themselves
from that tier's preset. Leave the cost options you want scaled unset; set the ones you want fixed.

```ts
import {Engine} from '@margoengine/core';
import {applyQualityTier, paceEngine, watchQuality} from '@margoengine/quality';
import {Shadows} from '@margoengine/shadows';
import {SSAO} from '@margoengine/post/ssao';

const tier = applyQualityTier();             // 'light' | 'high' | 'phone'; before the engine exists
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas, {backend: 'webgpu'});
paceEngine(engine);                          // light tier: a steady ~60 FPS instead of 120/40 swings

Shadows.attach(engine, {distance: 150});     // from the tier: 1024 + PCF light/phone (2 cascades on phones), 2048 + PCSS full
SSAO.attach(engine, {radius: 0.5});          // samples from the tier: 16 light/phone, 32 full
engine.start();
watchQuality();                              // measures the light tier; a fast GPU gets the full tier next load
console.log(tier);
```

What each tier does:

- **Light** (desktops until measured fast; `?quality=low` forces it): 1x MSAA, pixel ratio 1, paced to ~60 FPS, and the
  light preset (smaller shadow maps with four-tap PCF edges instead of PCSS, half the SSAO samples, SSR off, a coarser
  fog grid, smaller local shadow maps, 100,000 particles by default). The full table is in the
  [`@margoengine/quality` README](../../packages/quality/README.md#tier-presets).
- **Full** (`'high'`; `?quality=high` forces it): 4x MSAA and every package's own defaults.
- **Phone** (user agent): 1x MSAA, pixel ratio up to 2, the light preset with SSAO and volumetric fog off, two shadow
  cascades instead of four, and no scatter LOD fade (its `discard` turns off early depth rejection on phone GPUs).

Keep a value on every tier by passing it:

```ts
import {Shadows} from '@margoengine/shadows';
import {SSR} from '@margoengine/post/ssr';

Shadows.attach(engine, {resolution: 2048});   // explicit options always win over the preset
SSR.attach(engine, {enabled: true});          // SSR stays on even on the light tier (its steps still come from the tier)
```

Read the preset for your own settings, for example a particle-count menu:

```ts
import {qualityPreset, QUALITY_PRESETS} from '@margoengine/quality';

const particles = qualityPreset().vfx?.capacity ?? 1_000_000;   // 100,000 on light/phone, 1,000,000 on full
const lightShadow = QUALITY_PRESETS.light.shadows?.resolution;  // 1024
console.log(particles, lightShadow);
```

Notes:

- Apps without `@margoengine/quality` are unaffected: the packages read `globalThis.margoPreset` only, which nothing
  else sets.
- `localStorage['margoQuality:' + location.pathname]` holds `'high'` after a light-tier reading under `FAST_GPU_MS` (GPU passes by timestamp queries; without `timestamp-query` a page stays light), or `'held'` after the full tier ran slow. One key per page: the reading is what that page's scene costs. A slow light-tier reading stores nothing, so the next load measures again; `localStorage.removeItem('margoQuality:' + location.pathname)` clears either.
- Testing: `?quality=low|high` forces a tier without storing it; `?scale=1.5` raises the light tier's pixel ratio.

=== Kits (docs/guides/kits.md) ===

# Kits

A kit is one import line with the set of classes an app of one kind usually needs. It is part of `margoengine` (no
extra install), and it costs nothing you do not use: a bundler keeps only the names you import, so
`import {Shadows, createStage} from 'margoengine/game'` bundles the same bytes as importing them from their packages
(`tests/umbrella.test.js` compares the two).

<!-- Every ```ts block in this file is type-checked against the built packages by tests/from-threejs-snippets.test.js.
     Snippets may use the ambient names engine, canvas, mesh and model. -->

| Kit | For | Everything in it, at startup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `margoengine/game` | Games: models, animation, light and shadow, sky, physics, audio, input, effects | 327,526 B |
| `margoengine/viz` | Data and scientific visualization: figures and GPU compute, points, lines, splats, terrain, labels and text | 289,055 B |
| `margoengine/web` | Product viewers and 3D on web pages: a glTF model, studio light, orbit, HTML on top | 156,772 B |

The last column is min+gzip JavaScript with every name in the kit used, core and stage included (an app that uses
part of a kit pays for that part; core + stage alone is 22,815 B). Wasm decoders, workers and lazily loaded parts
are extra and load only when used. `tests/umbrella.test.js` measures these numbers on every run and fails when one
moves more than 3%.

Each kit also re-exports `createStage` and `Stage`, so a whole app can start from one line. Option types and the
rest of each package stay in that package: `import type {ShadowsOptions} from 'margoengine/shadows'`.

## A game in one import

```ts
import RAPIER from '@dimforge/rapier3d-compat';
import {Physics, Shadows, createStage} from 'margoengine/game';

await RAPIER.init();
const stage = await createStage('#viewport');
const physics = new Physics(stage.engine, {rapier: RAPIER});
const shadows = Shadows.attach(stage.engine, {resolution: 2048});
const floor = stage.box({size: [10, 1, 10], position: [0, -0.5, 0]});
const crate = stage.box({position: [0, 4, 0], color: '#c08040'});
physics.addBody(floor, {type: 'fixed'});
physics.addBody(crate, {colliders: {shape: 'box', restitution: 0.3}});
shadows.add(floor);
shadows.add(crate);
```

## Which kit

- Most apps start with a kit and add single packages (`margoengine/<package>`) for anything else.
- The kits overlap where apps overlap (orbit controls, the stage, post-processing); the same name is the same class
  in every kit.
- `npm create margo@latest my-game -- --template game` (or `viz`) starts an app from a kit.

## Contents

Generated from `scripts/umbrella.mjs` (`node scripts/umbrella.mjs` rewrites this section).

=== Prepare assets with margo-convert (docs/guides/asset-pipeline.md) ===

# Prepare assets with margo-convert

`margo-convert build` takes a folder of models and writes optimised copies, a manifest with hashes and sizes, and a
size report. One preset per place the assets are going: `web` (default), `mobile`, `unity`, `unreal`, `godot` and
`roblox`. Nothing to install beyond Node 22.12 or later:

```bash
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out dist
```

```text
built    Fox.glb
built    characters/Knight.glb
built    props/dagger.gltf

margo-convert web preset (sharp 0.35.5, ffmpeg not found)

file                   kind   status        in       out  saved
Fox.glb                model  built   162.9 kB   96.0 kB  41.1%
characters/Knight.glb  model  built   341.7 kB  145.1 kB  57.5%
props/dagger.gltf      model  built    25.7 kB   12.6 kB  51.0%

3 inputs: 3 built, 0 cached, 0 copied, 0 skipped, 0 failed
  model      3 files  530.3 kB -> 253.7 kB (52.2% saved)
total 530.3 kB -> 253.7 kB (52.2% saved)

notes
  Fox.glb: image 0: png recompressed (26764 -> 23403 bytes)
  characters/Knight.glb: image knight_texture: png -> webp (12914 -> 6242 bytes)
  props/dagger.gltf: image rogue_texture: png -> webp (15026 -> 7466 bytes)
```

(`dagger.gltf` is counted with the `.bin` and `.png` it reads, and is written as `props/dagger.glb`. Those files must
be in the model's folder or below it: a URI that leaves it (`../`, an absolute path, a drive or network path, or a
symlink that points out) fails that model with a `MargoError` of code `failed`.)

Run it again and every unchanged input says `cached`: an input is skipped when its content hash, the preset and the tool
version are the same and its outputs still match the manifest. `--force` rebuilds everything. A manifest that names an
output outside the output folder is treated as damaged: everything is rebuilt and nothing it names is deleted.

## What the manifest holds

`dist/margo-manifest.json` has one entry per input: relative path, size and SHA-256, a status (`built`, `cached`,
`copied` unchanged, `skipped`, `failed`), each output's path, size and SHA-256, notes (what was done, or what could not be
and why) and, for models, vertex and triangle counts before and after. It has no timestamps, so the same inputs give the
same manifest. Use it to upload only changed files, to set cache headers, or to find the hashed name of a file:

```bash
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out dist --hash-names   # Fox.fbdf9e94.glb, name chosen by content
```

```ts
import {loadGLTF} from '@margoengine/gltf-pro';

const manifest = await (await fetch('/dist/margo-manifest.json')).json();
const fox = manifest.files.find((f) => f.source === 'Fox.glb').outputs[0].path; // 'Fox.fbdf9e94.glb'
const loaded = await loadGLTF(engine, `/dist/${fox}`);
```

## One model

```bash
npx margo-convert optimize helmet.glb                 # helmet.optimized.glb, web preset
npx margo-convert optimize helmet.glb out/helmet.glb --preset unity
```

## Presets

Every preset prunes, dedupes and welds. They differ in what they assume about the reader.

### web

For a browser. Static meshes sharing a material are merged, positions are stored as 16-bit integers (the mesh bounds
move into the node transform), normals as 8-bit, and every vertex and index buffer is meshopt-compressed. The GLB
requires `KHR_mesh_quantization` and `EXT_meshopt_compression`, which Margo's loaders (`@margoengine/gltf-pro`) read; so
do other glTF loaders that support those extensions.

```bash
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out public/models
```

`Knight.glb` (character with a skin and a texture atlas) goes from 341,688 to 145,116 bytes. `RiggedFigure.glb` 50,116 to 29,340. `OrientationTest.glb`, a hierarchy of separate meshes, 38,920 to 18,520 with
them merged. Textures are where most of the bytes are: `BoomBox.glb` (2048 px PNG maps) goes from 10,614,184 to 4,131,040 bytes, `Lantern.glb` from 9,564,264 to 3,218,672 and `ToyCar.glb` from 5,422,412 to 2,396,924.

### mobile

The `web` model settings for phones: textures up to 1024 px at power-of-two sizes (so a GPU can block-compress and
mip them cleanly), WebP quality 72, and WAV audio mixed to mono at 22.05 kHz.

```bash
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out public/models --preset mobile
```

`BoomBox.glb` goes to 1,020,084 bytes (90% smaller), `Lantern.glb` to 990,848.

### unity, unreal, godot, roblox

Plain GLB with no required extension, no quantisation and no merging, so an importer sees what the artist made:
node hierarchy, empty nodes (often used as attachment points) and mesh names are kept. Duplicate materials, textures
and meshes are still merged and unused data still removed. Textures stay PNG or JPEG, at the sizes each engine wants:

| Preset | Largest texture | Sizes | Audio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unity` | 4096 px | multiples of 4 (block compression) | kept |
| `unreal` | 4096 px | powers of two (mip streaming) | kept |
| `godot` | 4096 px | any | kept |
| `roblox` | 1024 px | any | Ogg Vorbis with ffmpeg, otherwise WAV is reported: Roblox takes mp3 and ogg |

```bash
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out Assets/Models --preset unity
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out Content/Models --preset unreal
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out models --preset godot
npx margo-convert build ./assets --out upload --preset roblox
```

`BoomBox.glb` (2048 px PNG maps): `unity`, `unreal` and `godot` 6,451,548 bytes (the PNGs recompressed); `roblox`
1,643,508 (maps scaled to 1024 px).

Any setting can be changed for one run: `--max-texture 2048`, `--texture-format webp`, `--texture-quality 80`.

## Textures and audio on their own

Folders may hold plain textures and sounds next to models; `build` handles them with the same preset:

```bash
npx margo-convert build ./art --out public/art --preset mobile --mipmaps
```

`rock_normal.png` becomes a lossless `rock_normal.webp` (and a `rock_normal.dds` with its mip chain), `rock.png` a lossy
`rock.webp`, `zap.wav` a mono 22.05 kHz `zap.wav` (or `zap.ogg` when ffmpeg is installed). The size report ends with a
line per kind. sharp and ffmpeg are used only when already installed; the manifest's `encoders` says what was found.

## Thumbnails

`margo-convert thumbnail` renders a model to a PNG with no page. Install a WebGPU binding first: none ships with the
tool. Textured models also need sharp.

```sh
npm i webgpu sharp                                        # your choice of binding; sharp only for textured models
npx margo-convert thumbnail helmet.glb --out helmet.png --size 512
npx margo-convert thumbnail helmet.glb --out helmet.png --views front,iso   # helmet.front.png, helmet.iso.png
```

The options are in the [margo-convert README](../../tools/margo-convert/README.md#thumbnail). To render your own scene
from Node, use [`@margoengine/headless`](../../packages/headless/README.md).

## What is not done

- Draco compression: the repository has a Draco decoder only, no encoder. Meshopt is used instead.
- Level of detail: there is no mesh simplifier in the repository.
- KTX2 / Basis Universal textures: no encoder is installed.
- WebP, AVIF and JPEG need sharp, and Ogg Vorbis needs ffmpeg, already installed: without them PNG textures are
  recompressed and resized, and other images and audio pass through, with the reason in the manifest.
- Models that use `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `KHR_animation_pointer` or the metadata extensions are copied
  unchanged, with the reason in the manifest.

The reference for every option is the [margo-convert README](../../tools/margo-convert/README.md).

=== Coming from three.js (docs/from-threejs.md) ===

# Coming from three.js

A side-by-side guide for three.js developers. Each section shows the three.js code you already write, then the Margo
code that does the same job. Where Margo has no equivalent yet, the section says so; the full list is in
[Not yet](#not-yet).

     ```js blocks are three.js and are not checked. Snippets may use the ambient names engine, canvas, mesh and model. -->

## What is different

- **WebGPU first.** Core renders with WebGPU. The WebGL2 fallback is the optional `@margoengine/webgl` package and
  draws core meshes only (flat PBR, one light, no textures or effects). Most optional packages need WebGPU.
- **No `Scene` object.** One `Engine` owns one canvas, one camera and one implicit scene. Meshes are created by the
  engine (`engine.createMesh()`), and features (shadows, lights, post effects, controls) are plugins you attach with
  one form, `X.attach(engine, options)` (async ones such as `Environment.attach` return a Promise). A loaded model
  joins a feature with `feature.add(model)`. Everything disposable has `dispose()`, and every package object also has
  `[Symbol.dispose]` for `using` (core's `Engine` and meshes and the stage facade have `dispose()` only).
- **Small core, optional packages.** Core plus the `margoengine` stage facade is about 21 kB gzip (`npm run measure:size` prints the exact figure;
  WebGPU only). The smallest lit-box app is about 130 kB gzip with three.js 0.186's WebGLRenderer and
  212 kB with its WebGPURenderer, built the same way ([threejs-size.json](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/threejs-size.json);
  `npm run bench -- size --engines=all` remeasures it from engine-bench). Everything else is a separate
  package that you install and import only when you use it.
- **Tuples, not classes.** Positions, colours and directions are plain arrays (`[x, y, z]`, `'#rrggbb'`). A three.js-style
  math library exists (`@margoengine/math`) and converts with `toArray()`.
- **The camera is a position and a target.** `camera.up` sets screen up (so exact top-down views work) and
  `camera.project` replaces the projection; `@margoengine/cameras` uses both for orthographic views.
- **Resize and pixel ratio are automatic.** The engine sizes its drawing buffer from the canvas's CSS size every frame.
  Desktops render with 4x MSAA at pixel ratio 1, phones single-sampled at up to 2. `@margoengine/quality` measures the
  GPU and picks a lighter tier on slow machines.
- **Colours.** `'#rrggbb'` strings are sRGB and converted to linear, as `new THREE.Color('#...')` does; number arrays are
  linear RGB. Output is tone mapped and sRGB-encoded for you.
- **Two levels of mesh.** Core meshes are position + normal geometry with a constant PBR material, instanced
  automatically. Textured meshes and loaded glTF models are drawn by `@margoengine/gltf-pro` (through
  `@margoengine/materials` for meshes you build). Shadows, clustered lights and SSAO light core meshes automatically
  and need `add(model)` for gltf-pro models.

## Install only what you import

Each row is a separate npm package (not published yet: until then, build from source with `npm ci && npm run build:packages`). Install the ones you import; bundlers drop the rest.

```sh
npm install @margoengine/core                      # engine, camera, meshes, constant PBR material
npm install margoengine                            # optional facade: createStage('#app'), app.box(), addGLTF(app, url)
npm install @margoengine/geometry @margoengine/materials @margoengine/gltf-pro @margoengine/controls
```

| You use in three.js | Margo package |
| --- | --- |
| `WebGLRenderer`, `PerspectiveCamera`, `Mesh`, `MeshStandardMaterial` (colour only) | `@margoengine/core` |
| WebGL fallback | `@margoengine/webgl` |
| `BoxGeometry`, `SphereGeometry`, `ExtrudeGeometry`, `BufferGeometryUtils` | `@margoengine/geometry` |
| `TextureLoader`, `MeshStandardMaterial` with maps and the other mesh materials | `@margoengine/materials` |
| `GLTFLoader` (textured, extensions) | `@margoengine/gltf-pro` (+ `@margoengine/decoders` for Draco, meshopt, KTX2) |
| `FBXLoader`, `USDZLoader`, `PLYLoader`/`PCDLoader`/`3MFLoader`, `STLLoader`/`OBJLoader` | `@margoengine/fbx`, `@margoengine/usdz`, `@margoengine/loaders` |
| `AnimationMixer`, skinning, morphs | `@margoengine/animation` (+ `@margoengine/animator` for blending) |
| `DirectionalLight` shadows | `@margoengine/shadows` |
| `PointLight`, `SpotLight` (and their shadows) | `@margoengine/clustered` (shadows: `@margoengine/clustered/shadows`) |
| `RectAreaLight` | `@margoengine/clustered/area` |
| `RGBELoader`, `EXRLoader`, `PMREMGenerator`, `scene.background`, `scene.fog` | `@margoengine/environment` |
| Volumetric fog and light shafts (`VolumeNodeMaterial`) | `@margoengine/environment/volumetric` |
| `Sky` add-on | `@margoengine/sky` |
| `OrbitControls`, `TransformControls`, `DragControls`, `FlyControls`, ... | `@margoengine/controls` |
| `Raycaster`, three-mesh-bvh | `@margoengine/bvh` |
| GPU picking, `OutlinePass` | `@margoengine/selection` |
| `LOD` | `@margoengine/lod` |
| `EffectComposer`, `UnrealBloomPass`, `SSAOPass`, `FXAAShader` | `@margoengine/post` |
| `BokehPass` | `@margoengine/dof` |
| `OutputPass`, tone mapping, `LUTPass` | `@margoengine/tonemap` |
| `TAARenderPass` | `@margoengine/taa` |
| TSL, node materials | `@margoengine/shader` |
| `OrthographicCamera` | `@margoengine/cameras` |
| `Line2`, `LineMaterial`, `GridHelper`, `AxesHelper` | `@margoengine/lines` |
| `vector.project(camera)`, `vector.unproject(camera)` | `projectPoint(v, engine.camera, v)`, `unprojectPoint(v, engine.camera, v)` from `@margoengine/math`, plus `worldToScreen` and `screenToWorld` for pixels. A point behind the camera returns null, and on WebGPU depth runs near = 1 to far = 0 |
| `SphericalHarmonics3` | `SH3` from `@margoengine/math` (also `@margoengine/math/sh`); `getAt`, `getIrradianceAt` and `addScaledSH` keep their names, colours are `{r, g, b}` |
| `ColorManagement.convert` | `convertColor(rgb, from, to)` from `@margoengine/math` (also `@margoengine/math/color-space`), with `SRGBColorSpace` and the other named spaces |
| `Capsule` (addons `math/Capsule.js`) | `Capsule` from `@margoengine/math` (also `@margoengine/math/capsule`); `pushOutOfTriangle` gives the move a character needs |
| `Points`, `Sprite` | `@margoengine/points` |
| troika-three-text | `@margoengine/text` |
| `CSS2DRenderer`, `CSS3DRenderer` | `@margoengine/labels` (`@margoengine/html` adds depth occlusion) |
| `Vector3`, `Matrix4`, `Quaternion`, `Color`, `Box3`, `Line3`, `Triangle`, `Cylindrical`, `OBB` (addons `math/OBB.js`) | `@margoengine/math` (each also as its own entry, such as `@margoengine/math/obb`; `Cylindrical` turns into a point with `toVector3(out)`, there is no `Vector3.setFromCylindrical`) |
| stats.js | `@margoengine/stats` |
| `renderer.info`, Spector.js, lil-gui scene inspectors | `@margoengine/inspector` (`@margoengine/inspector/frame`: frame debugger) |
| `ViewHelper` | `@margoengine/viewcube` |
| ContactShadows example (product-shot ground shadow) | `@margoengine/staging` |
| react-three-fiber | `@margoengine/react` |

Feature entries keep bundles smaller still: `@margoengine/post/ssao`, `@margoengine/post/bloom`,
`@margoengine/post/stack`, `@margoengine/post/fxaa`, `@margoengine/animation/vat`, `@margoengine/sky/base` load one feature without the rest of their package.

## Renderer, scene, camera and resize

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({antialias: true});
renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2));
renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight);
document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
const scene = new THREE.Scene();
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(60, innerWidth / innerHeight, 0.1, 1000);
camera.position.set(0, 2, 5);
camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0);
addEventListener('resize', () => {
  camera.aspect = innerWidth / innerHeight;
  camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight);
});
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => renderer.render(scene, camera));
```

```ts
import {Engine} from '@margoengine/core';
import {webglRenderer} from '@margoengine/webgl'; // optional: only if you want a WebGL2 fallback

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas'); // give it a CSS size, e.g. width: 100%; height: 100vh
const engine = await Engine.create(canvas, {
  camera: {position: [0, 2, 5], target: [0, 0, 0], fov: 60, near: 0.1, far: 1000},
  fallback: webglRenderer,
});
engine.start(); // resize, pixel ratio and MSAA are handled per frame
```

Or with the stage facade, which also creates the canvas, attaches CAD-style camera controls and starts rendering:

```ts
import {createStage} from 'margoengine';
const app = await createStage('#scene'); // a container element with a height
app.box({size: [1, 1, 1], color: '#84d6bd'});
```

- `engine.camera` has `position`, `target`, `fov`, `near`, `far` and `up`. Assign a new tuple to move it
  (`engine.camera.position = [4, 3, 6]`); there is no `lookAt`, the target is the look-at point.
- `engine.camera.fitToBoundingBox(min, max, {duration: 0.3})` frames a box, animated. `@margoengine/cameras`'
  `projection.fit(model.bounds)` takes the flat bounds array and also fits orthographic views (by zoom).
- `engine.backend` is `'webgpu'` or `'webgl2'`; `engine.fallbackReason` says why WebGPU was not used.
- `capacity` (default 1,024) is the initial number of meshes and transform nodes an engine holds; `createMesh` doubles it
  when full, up to 8,388,608. Set it for big scenes to skip the doublings: `Engine.create(canvas, {capacity: 50_000})`.
- Each engine owns one implicit scene. `engine.render({camera})` supports sequential alternate-camera captures, and
  `core/extension` exposes per-core-draw viewport/scissor rectangles. Optional native passes and picking do not inherit
  those rectangles.

A transparent canvas over HTML and CSS, like `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({alpha: true})` with `setClearColor(0x000000, 0)`:

```ts
import {Engine} from '@margoengine/core';
import {TransparentCanvas} from '@margoengine/environment';
import {webglRenderer} from '@margoengine/webgl';

const overlay = await Engine.create(canvas, {fallback: c => webglRenderer(c, {transparent: true})}); // WebGL fallback: transparent too
TransparentCanvas.attach(overlay); // WebGPU: premultiplied canvas, alpha 0 where nothing is drawn
```

FXAA, Bloom and `PostStack` keep the alpha; Tonemap and SSAO keep it with a faint rim on silhouettes; DOF, TAA,
SceneFade and the other backgrounds make the canvas opaque again (`@margoengine/post` README).

Display P3 and HDR output, like `renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.DisplayP3ColorSpace` and the WebGPU renderer's
extended tone mapping:

```ts
import {ColorOutput} from '@margoengine/environment';
import {Tonemap} from '@margoengine/tonemap';

const output = ColorOutput.attach(engine, {gamut: 'p3', hdr: true, peak: 4}); // only where the display reports P3 / HDR
Tonemap.attach(engine, {curve: 'neutral'}); // highlights above white and colours outside sRGB come from Tonemap
console.log(output.gamut, output.hdr); // what the canvas really is ('srgb' and false on an sRGB/SDR display)
```

sRGB content looks the same on the P3 canvas (as three.js converts sRGB colours for a P3 output). There is no
ColorManagement API: colours and textures are sRGB (environment README, "Display P3 and HDR output").

## Meshes and geometry

```js
const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({color: '#84d6bd', roughness: 0.3}));
mesh.position.set(0, 0.5, 0);
mesh.rotation.y = Math.PI / 4;
scene.add(mesh);
const group = new THREE.Group();
group.add(mesh);
```

```ts
import {box, PbrMaterial} from '@margoengine/core';

const mesh = engine.createMesh()
  .setGeometry(box(1, 1, 1))
  .setMaterial(new PbrMaterial({color: '#84d6bd', roughness: 0.3, metalness: 0}));
mesh.position.set(0, 0.5, 0);
mesh.rotation.y = Math.PI / 4; // Euler XYZ in radians; setQuaternion([x, y, z, w]) also works
const group = engine.createMesh(); // a mesh without geometry is a transform node
mesh.setParent(group);
mesh.visible = false;
```

Every three.js primitive is in `@margoengine/geometry`, with the same parameters and defaults (vertex
order is our own and not part of the API). They return plain typed arrays; `toGeometry` hands them to core.

```js
const sphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 32, 16);
const torus = new THREE.TorusKnotGeometry(1, 0.3, 128, 16);
const shape = new THREE.Shape().moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(2, 0).lineTo(2, 1).lineTo(0, 1);
const extruded = new THREE.ExtrudeGeometry(shape, {depth: 0.4, bevelEnabled: false});
```

```ts
import {PbrMaterial} from '@margoengine/core';
import {sphereGeometry, torusKnotGeometry, planeGeometry, Shape, extrudeGeometry, mergeGeometries, toGeometry} from '@margoengine/geometry';

const sphere = toGeometry(sphereGeometry(1, 32, 16));
const torus = toGeometry(torusKnotGeometry(1, 0.3, 128, 16));
const plane = planeGeometry(10, 10); // uvs and tangents stay on the data for @margoengine/materials
const shape = new Shape([[0, 0], [2, 0], [2, 1], [0, 1]]);
const extruded = toGeometry(extrudeGeometry(shape, {depth: 0.4, bevelEnabled: false}));
engine.createMesh().setGeometry(sphere).setMaterial(new PbrMaterial({color: '#f97316'}));
```

Custom geometry: `new Geometry(positions, normals, indices)` from core. Core geometry has no UVs or vertex colours and is
immutable once attached; build a new `Geometry` to change it. For UVs, vertex colours and textures, use
`@margoengine/materials` (next section).

## Materials and textures

Core's `PbrMaterial` is colour, roughness, metalness and `doubleSided`. Textures, transparency and the other shading
models come from `@margoengine/materials`, which draws through gltf-pro (WebGPU only).

Core materials are live, like three.js's `material.color.set(...)`: `set` changes the given values in place and every
mesh using the material shows them on the next frame (no new material, pipeline or bind group).

```js
mesh.material.color.set('#ff8800');
mesh.material.roughness = 0.2;
```

```ts
import {PbrMaterial} from '@margoengine/core';

const paint = new PbrMaterial({color: '#84d6bd'});
mesh.setMaterial(paint);
paint.set({color: '#ff8800', roughness: 0.2}); // omitted values keep theirs; invalid input throws and changes nothing
```

```js
const map = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('/crate.jpg');
map.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
map.wrapS = map.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping;
map.repeat.set(2, 2);
const crate = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({map, normalMap, roughness: 0.7}));
const screen = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1.6, 0.9), new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({map: new THREE.VideoTexture(video)}));
const glass = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({color: '#88ccff', transparent: true, opacity: 0.4, side: THREE.DoubleSide});
```

```ts
import {boxGeometry, planeGeometry} from '@margoengine/geometry';
import {loadTexture, Texture, PbrMaterial, UnlitMaterial, createMesh} from '@margoengine/materials';

const map = await loadTexture('/crate.jpg', {wrapS: 'repeat', wrapT: 'repeat', anisotropy: 8}); // colour maps read sRGB
const normalMap = await loadTexture('/crate-normal.png');                                        // other slots linear
const crate = createMesh(engine, boxGeometry(1, 1, 1), new PbrMaterial({
  map, normalMap, roughness: 0.7,
  uvTransform: {offset: [0, 0], scale: [2, 2], rotation: 0}, // map.repeat / offset / rotation
}));
crate.root.setPosition([0, 0.5, 0]);
const video = document.querySelector('video');
createMesh(engine, planeGeometry(1.6, 0.9), new UnlitMaterial({map: new Texture(video)}));
const glass = new PbrMaterial({color: '#88ccff', transparent: true, opacity: 0.4, side: 'double'});
createMesh(engine, planeGeometry(2, 2), glass, {renderOrder: 1});
glass.opacity = 0.6; // colours, scalars and maps are live
```

One class per three.js mesh material, each a `Material` with its shading fixed (`new Material({shading})` also works):
